name: Parsley
description: Parsley represents a highly dense vegetative phytomatrix belonging to the Apiaceae family, characterized by an exceptional concentration of structural lipophilic quinones, water-soluble reducing agents, and specific flavone glycosides. It acts as an active modulator of renal aquaporin channels and a potent inhibitor of vascular inflammatory signaling pathways. This distinct botanical matrix systematically enhances endothelial nitric oxide production, regulates extracellular fluid homeostasis through targeted osmotic shifts, and fortifies the structural integrity of the skeletal collagen matrix.
macroIntro: The macronutrient configuration of fresh parsley displays a minimal thermodynamic footprint, exhibiting an optimized ratio of nitrogenous plant proteins and non-starch structural fibers with negligible metabolic resistance.
microIntro: As a highly specialized photosynthetic bio-reservoir, parsley greens concentrate volatile secondary metabolites, vital transition metals, and essential mineral cofactors necessary for preserving vascular tone and immune homeostasis.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: A very low energy payload that enables unrestricted volumetric dietary integration without triggering adipocyte hypertrophy or postprandial glycemic volatility.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Composed of structurally diverse plant polypeptides and free amino acids, offering an efficient amino-acid enrichment for basic metabolic repair cycles.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: A minor lipid profile, primarily comprising functional monoterpene fractions, polyunsaturated fatty acids, and essential surface membrane lipids.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Represented by a complex polysaccharide framework interwoven with insoluble fiber matrices, ensuring a slow, controlled carbohydrate release curve.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K (Phylloquinone)
microNutrients.description: An exceptional concentration of lipophilic cofactor required for gamma-glutamyl carboxylase activity, driving the activation of hepatic coagulation factors and osteocalcin synthesis.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C (L-Ascorbic Acid)
microNutrients.description: An outstanding water-soluble reducing agent that drives leukocyte tracking, accelerates dermal extracellular matrix cross-linking, and provides direct cellular free-radical neutralization.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin A (as Beta-Carotene)
microNutrients.description: A highly concentrated lipophilic provitamin essential for target nuclear gene transcription, secretory epithelial differentiation, and retinal opsin regeneration cycles.

microNutrients.name: Iron
microNutrients.description: A critical transition metal payload serving as the central coordination complex in non-heme metalloproteins, supporting regular erythrocyte hemoglobin synthesis and systemic oxygen delivery.

microNutrients.name: Apigenin
microNutrients.description: A dominant flavone aglycone that suppresses inflammatory cytokine expression via NF-kB pathway inhibition while demonstrating potential competitive binding to central GABA-A receptors.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: A vital intracellular electrolyte regulating myofibrillar resting membrane potentials, counteracting sodium-induced intracellular hypervolemia, and optimizing blood pressure dynamics.

healthBenefits: Cardiovascular Protection and Homocysteine Regulation: Apigenin and essential folate cofactors downregulate vascular cell adhesion molecules (VCAM-1) and accelerate the conversion of pro-thrombotic homocysteine to methionine, preserving long-term arterial elasticity.

Osmotic Diuretic and Aquaporin Modulation: Active volatile compounds (myristicin and apiol) induce mild renal tissue irritation, inhibiting the basolateral $Na^+/K^+$-ATPase pump in the proximal convoluted tubules to increase urine output and optimize extracellular fluid distribution.

Osteoblast Activation and Bone Mineralization: The profound saturation of phylloquinone acts as a direct molecular switch for the gamma-carboxylation of osteocalcin, enabling precise calcium ion fixation within the crystalline hydroxyapatite bone matrix.

Mitochondrial Protection and Radical Defense: The high-density integration of L-ascorbic acid and beta-carotene acts as a multi-layered redox buffer, neutralizing hydroxyl and superoxide radicals to prevent cellular DNA mutations.
precautionsIntro: Despite its excellent culinary safety profile, the pharmacological and biochemical density of parsley warrants clinical screening under certain medical or physiological parameters.
precautions: Uterine Smooth Muscle Activation: Pharmacological or concentrated supplemental extractions of parsley are strictly contraindicated during gestation, as high doses of volatile apiol and myristicin act as potent myometrial stimulants capable of inducing uterine hypertonicity.

Oxalate-Mediated Renal Nephrolithiasis: Parsley contains a notable concentration of organic oxalic acid salts; excessive and continuous consumption can accelerate the precipitation of insoluble calcium oxalate crystals within the renal collecting tubules.

Competitive Interaction with Anticoagulants: Due to the extreme density of phylloquinone (Vitamin K), high dietary intake directly antagonizes vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKORC1), severely dampening the therapeutic efficacy of coumarin-based oral anticoagulants like warfarin.

Apiaceae Family Cross-Reactive Allergenicity: Specific structural proteins within parsley can act as direct airborne or dietary antigens, inducing IgE-mediated cross-sensitization (Oral Allergy Syndrome) in patients displaying established clinical hypersensitivity to celery, carrot, or coriander.
